intro: Now you write it. The sentence starter is the same one on your Make the Case page — use it. Getting used to it now is how it becomes automatic in June, when every point on the Regents essay counts.
prompt: You have the evidence. Now explain it: what does it show, and why does that matter?
checklist: Says what the evidence shows, in your own words
Says why it matters (“which matters because”)
model_response: This shows expansion was being argued as something the country was owed rather than something it chose, which matters because an argument like that leaves nobody to answer to — not Mexico, and not the people already living on the land.

source_document: Document 8 — “Annexation,” United States Magazine and Democratic Review, 1845, attributed to John L. O'Sullivan (adapted)
source_text: . . . other nations have undertaken to intrude themselves into it [the question of Texas], between us and the proper parties to the case, in a spirit of hostile interference against us, for the avowed [openly stated] object of thwarting [blocking] our policy and hampering our power, limiting our greatness and checking the fulfillment of our manifest destiny to overspread the continent allotted by Providence [God] for the free development of our yearly multiplying millions. . . .
